description: Each country's emissions of all greenhouse gases from all sectors on its territory, including net land use, divided by its population (the world's value also counts international aviation and shipping, which FAO counts in no country), in tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent per person per year, as published by FAO since 1990. This is a national average where emissions happen, not one person's footprint: it does not follow what people buy (emissions in imported goods count where they are made) and says nothing about how emissions differ between people in a country. FAO has no row for some sectors of three territories (November 2026 release), so their values leave those sectors out: Mayotte has no energy, industry, waste or other emissions, Tokelau no energy or other, and Nauru no other. Values can be below zero where forests take up more carbon than the country emits: 201 of the values in the November 2026 release are.

processing.description: Read Climate_change_Emissions_indicators_E_All_Data_(Normalized).csv from FAOSTAT's Emissions indicators (EM) bulk zip. The vintage is the domain's DateUpdate, 6 November 2026, from FAOSTAT's bulk-download catalogue (datasets_E.json), whose entry names this zip and gives FileRows 744,060, the number of data rows in this file. The zip was last modified on the server on Fri, 06 Nov 2026 16:55:13 GMT.

Kept the rows of item "All sectors with LULUCF" (code 6825), element "Emissions per capita" (code 7279), unit "t CO2eq/cap", 1990–2024, as FAO prints them. FAO divides each area's all-sector emissions by its population; nothing is computed here.

201 published per-person values are below zero, in 20 areas (ALB, BDI, BIH, BLR, BTN, COK, CRI, ECU, FIN, FJI, GHA, HND, LAO, LCA, LVA, MNE, NIU, RWA, SWE, VNM), where land use, land-use change and forestry takes up more carbon than the other emissions counted add up to; the lowest is MNE 2009 (-25.2023 t CO2eq/cap as printed). Published as printed.

Left out former states and territories reported only before their dissolution, with no entity here (Belgium-Luxembourg, Czechoslovakia, Ethiopia PDR, Pacific Islands Trust Territory, Sudan (former), USSR, Yugoslav SFR); FAO regional and analytical groups (Africa, Americas, Annex I countries, Asia, Australia and New Zealand, Caribbean, Central America, Central Asia, China, Eastern Africa, Eastern Asia, Eastern Europe, Europe, Land Locked Developing Countries (LLDCs), Least Developed Countries (LDCs), Low Income Food Deficit Countries (LIFDCs), Melanesia, Micronesia, Middle Africa, Net Food Importing Developing Countries (NFIDCs), Non-Annex I countries, Northern Africa, Northern America, Northern Europe, OECD, Oceania, Polynesia, Small Island Developing States (SIDS), South America, South-eastern Asia, Southern Africa, Southern Asia, Southern Europe, Western Africa, Western Asia, Western Europe). Their values are never re-assigned to other entities.
Every value used carries FAO's flag E, which the file's codebook defines as "Estimated value".

Left out the rows FAO prints with no value and flag L ("Missing value; data exist but were not collected"): Nicaragua 2023, 2024. Those areas and years stay missing; nothing is filled in or set to zero.

scope.basis: FAO's published value of all-sector emissions (FAOSTAT item "All sectors with LULUCF") divided by population, territorial (production-based) accounting. FAOSTAT's six IPCC sectors: energy, industrial processes and product use, agriculture, land use, land-use change and forestry (net: emissions from deforestation, drained organic soils and fires minus the carbon taken up by existing forests, so it can be negative), waste and other. International aviation and shipping (bunker fuels) are counted in the World's total only, as a part of their own, since FAO's release of 6 November 2026; no country's total includes them. Agriculture and land use are FAO's own Tier 1 estimates; energy, industry, waste and other are PRIMAP-hist v2.8 third-party estimates, which count some territories inside their parent country (for example Bermuda in the United Kingdom, Greenland and the Faroe Islands in Denmark, Palestine in Israel, Puerto Rico in the United States). So such a parent country's energy, industry, waste and other emissions include those territories while its agriculture and land use do not, and for 27 territories in the November 2026 release FAO has no energy, industry, waste or other rows, so their total covers agriculture and land use only. Estimates, not country inventory submissions.
